import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 42: Maximal Sidon Sets and Disjoint Difference Sets

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/42](https://www.erdosproblems.com/42)

This problem asks whether maximal Sidon sets can coexist with other Sidon sets that have
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).
-/

open Function Set Filter
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos42

/--
**Erdős Problem 42**: Let M ≥ 1 and N be sufficiently large in terms of M. Is it true that for every
maximal Sidon set `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` there is another Sidon set `B ⊆ {1,…,N}` of size M such that
`(A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`?

This was proved for all $M$ by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Sandhu), see discussion thread for more details.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Shashi456/erdos-formalizations/blob/main/Erdos/P42/CompactCayley/Proof.lean"]
theorem erdos_42 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N),
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
    ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0} := by
  sorry

/--
A variant asking for explicit bounds on how large N needs to be in terms of M.

This version provides a constructive function f such that for all M ≥ 1 and N ≥ f(M),
every maximal Sidon set A ⊆ {1,…,N} has another Sidon set B ⊆ {1,…,N} of size M with
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-42-constructive-variant/blob/1f82c76be43cb56f22e2f7f792e392d5fb3ff78c/lean/Erdos42Constructive.lean"]
theorem erdos_42.variants.constructive : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (M N : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ M) (_ : f M ≤ N),
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N), ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ),
      B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
      ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0} := by
  sorry


/-  ## Related results and examples -/

/--
The set `{1, 2, 4}` is a maximal Sidon set in `{1, ..., 4}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_maximal_sidon : IsMaximalSidonSetIn {1, 2, 4} 4 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp [Set.mem_Icc]
  · intro i₁ hi₁ j₁ hj₁ i₂ hi₂ j₂ hj₂ hsum
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi₁ hj₁ hi₂ hj₂
    rcases hi₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hj₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hi₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hj₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    simp_all
  · intro x hx hxA
    simp only [Set.mem_Icc] at hx; obtain ⟨hx1, hx2⟩ := hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, not_or] at hxA
    obtain ⟨hne1, hne2, hne4⟩ := hxA
    have hx3 : x = 3 := (by omega); subst hx3
    intro hbad
    have := hbad 1 (by simp) 2 (by simp) 3 (by simp) 2 (by simp) (by norm_num)
    rcases this with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩ <;> omega

/--
The difference set of `{1, 2, 4}` is `{0, 1, 2, 3}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_difference_set : ({1, 2, 4} : Set ℕ) - {1, 2, 4} = {0, 1, 2, 3} := by
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_sub, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
    rcases ha with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    simp
  · rintro (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl)
    · exact ⟨1, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨2, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨4, by decide, 2, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨4, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩

/--
For any maximal Sidon set, the difference set contains 0.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem maximal_sidon_contains_zero (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hA : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N) : 0 ∈ A - A := by
  obtain ⟨hAsub, hAsidon, hAmax⟩ := hA
  have hne : A.Nonempty
  · by_contra hemp; rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at hemp
    exact hAmax (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨le_refl 1, hN⟩)
      (by rw [hemp]; exact id) (by
        rw [hemp, Set.empty_union]
        exact fun _ hi _ hj _ hk _ hl _ => by
          simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi hj hk hl
          subst hi
          subst hj
          subst hk
          subst hl
          exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
  have := Set.sub_mem_sub ha ha
  rwa [Nat.sub_self] at this

end Erdos42

findings.description: The docstring at lines 48–52 advertises “explicit bounds” and a “constructive function f,” but the statement only asserts `∃ f : ℕ → ℕ` satisfying the threshold property. It specifies neither a bound nor any effectiveness requirement. This proposition follows from the main eventual statement by classical choice; it is a faithful equivalent formulation of the qualitative problem, not the quantitative result advertised in the docstring.
findings.source_evidence: The exact cited proof, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KitaKen1/erdos-42-constructive-variant/1f82c76be43cb56f22e2f7f792e392d5fb3ff78c/lean/Erdos42Constructive.lean, explicitly states: “Classical choice selects one threshold for each M” and “This is an existence proof. It does not compute an explicit numerical bound.” Its proof uses `eventually_atTop` and `choose f hf`. The main source, https://www.erdosproblems.com/42, asks for N sufficiently large in terms of M.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe this as an equivalent threshold-function formulation asserting the existence of f, and remove the promises of explicit bounds and constructivity. A genuinely quantitative variant should separately specify or ask for an explicit bound.

reformulations.difference: The current problem page quantifies over every Sidon subset, while Lean quantifies only over inclusion-maximal Sidon subsets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every Sidon subset A of the finite interval has an inclusion-maximal Sidon extension C in the same interval. Any B avoiding all nonzero differences of C also avoids those of A. For nonempty A and B, zero remains in both difference sets, giving the required equality rather than merely containment in {0}. Conversely, the all-Sidon statement includes maximal sets. Maximal sets are nonempty when N ≥ 1, which may be imposed eventually. The source's M=1 explanation explicitly assumes A nonempty, and its discussion confirms the inclusion-maximal reduction. I proved maximal extension and the eventual equivalence in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` (`exists_maximal_extension`, `all_nonempty_eventual_iff`), without using either admitted research theorem. This argument does not require extension to a maximum-cardinality Sidon set.

reformulations.difference: Both research declarations form the difference sets in `Set ℕ`, using truncated subtraction, rather than signed integer subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A common positive natural difference is exactly a common positive integer difference. Any common negative integer difference gives a common positive difference after reversing both ordered pairs. Thus the absence of common nonzero differences is unchanged. Zero belongs to both self-difference sets when the sets are nonempty; here maximality ensures this for A once N ≥ 1, and `B.ncard = M ≥ 1` ensures it for B. I proved the precise set-equality equivalence under the cast ℕ → ℤ in `Review42.truncated_vs_integer_differences`, and also checked that the Sidon predicate is preserved by this cast. The primary paper's formulation using differences with i < j likewise only tests positive differences.

reformulations.difference: The variant replaces “for each M ≥ 1, eventually in N” by existence of a single threshold function `f : ℕ → ℕ`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, `Filter.eventually_atTop` identifies eventual truth with existence of a threshold n₀ after which the predicate always holds. Classical choice selects such a threshold for each positive M; f(0) can be arbitrary because the condition requires 1 ≤ M. Conversely, f(M) supplies the eventual threshold for each M. I proved this ↔ for the exact witness property in `Review42.threshold_iff_eventual`. It is equivalent to the qualitative question, without asserting an explicit numerical bound.

review.notes: All five declarations were checked; no substantive mathematical misformalization was found. The original 1995 paper says “maximum Sidon sequence,” whereas the current cited problem page poses the more general all-Sidon question; the maximality equivalence above is to that current formulation. The source discussion explicitly uses nonempty A, avoiding the impossible literal empty-set case of equality to {0}. Finiteness follows from containment in Icc, so `ncard`'s infinite-set default is unreachable. Scratch tests cover N=0, M=0, M=1, and exhaustive finite examples for N=0,…,9. The three textbook proofs have only standard axioms. The scratch equivalences and the bridge to the external proof's predicates compile without sorry. I inspected both cited proof statements and found no custom axioms or proof holes in their source. A full replay of the large external proof failed on Mathlib API changes in the sandbox's Lean 4.33.1 environment; the source announcement reports checking it with Mathlib 4.28. This replay limitation is not evidence against its recorded proof status. The reviewed file's hash still matches the committed version.
